value.rationale: This solves the natural unbiased two-call oracle pairing decision completely on the smallest nontrivial finite-sum bilinear game, not merely a renamed stable-rate bound. A sharp heterogeneity threshold selects antithetic versus shared pairing for maximal admissible step, while same-sample remains best at jointly optimized contraction. The exact rational example demonstrates that antithetic pairing converges when both conventional shared and independent pairing diverge at equal two-call cost. It provides a meaningful reference counterexample and motivates further multi-component coupling designs without claiming their solution.
